Summary  
Data source overview: A brief MIRI-authored text argues that 1) catastrophic AI misalignment remains the central risk; 2) purely technical alignment is extremely hard and unsolved; 3) policy fixes are viewed as even less promising; 4) therefore MIRI funds many independent researchers who pursue mathematically-formal, security-mindset approaches to alignment, hoping that at least one line of work will succeed.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE [71] – Short source limits detail, but paths are faithfully reconstructed and strictly respect required node/edge patterns and checklist rules.  
Inference strategy justification: Because the text is only a paragraph, moderate inference (confidence ≤ 2) was applied to supply missing implementation mechanisms, validation analogues and concrete interventions that an AI-safety researcher would naturally derive (formal-methods programmes, independent-research funding). All such links are flagged with edge confidence 2 and rationale notes.  
Extraction completeness explanation: Every explicit claim in the paragraph is represented, augmented with two inferred but well-supported causal-interventional chains, ensuring a fully connected fabric from the single top-level risk to two actionable interventions.  
Key limitations: 1) No quantitative evidence in source – validation nodes rely on domain analogies; 2) Only high-level interventions are supported; 3) Security-mindset decomposition might omit finer sub-components present in longer writings.
